text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Hosted API p95/p99 latency spike detected in us-east-1. Request queue growth +45% over 10m. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale actions, 2 failures. Paging oncall. (alert id: A-3301-queue)
maria (oncall): acked. seeing user reports of timeouts. hit the dashboard, p95 -> 1.6s -> 4.3s, p99 -> 5.8s -> 18.2s. queues: backend-request-queue length 9k -> 18k in last 12m. any deploys? :eyes:
sam (runtime): no prod deploys from runtime team in last hour. telemetry shows GPU pool saturating (pool gpu-hosted-1). Autoscaler logs show failures during instance create: provider returned quota_exceeded and rate_limit. grabbing logs now.
tiago (provisioning): seeing throttles from cloud provider in provisioner logs. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T04:25:11Z provisioner: create_instance(us-east-1, type=gpu-v3) -> 429 QuotaExceeded: "GPUs quota reached for project"
2026-03-15T04:26:03Z provisioner: retry(1)
2026-03-15T04:26:35Z provisioner: create_instance -> 429 RateLimit
```
alice (sre): ok, that's the root cause for scale fails. while we sort quota, we need immediate mitigations to reduce customer impact. suggestions: 1) enable fallback routing to smaller-quantized models (cpu/low-gpu), 2) apply soft global rate limit to newcomers, 3) enable prefix cache to reduce token churn, 4) temporarily increase request timeouts for clients? (maybe avoid retries)
maria (oncall): priority order please. also need comms: CS and product notified.
kevin (product): product + cs here. impact assessment: we have 14 customers with >1% of traffic in the affected region; 3 customers are reporting failed inference calls (timeouts). please call out customers with p99>10s for cs to triage.
sam (runtime): running async plan now. actions I'm starting: 1) flip routing policy to prefer quantized-v2-small model for standard tier (non-enterprise) for us-east-1. 2) enable cache warmup for the top 50 prefixes for top callers. 3) set autoscaler to manual burst = 0 (stop further retries that hammer provider).
commands:
```
# route standard traffic to quantized fallback
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood/api/routes/route-change \
  -d '{"region":"us-east-1","selector":"tier:standard","target_model":"quantized-v2-small"}'

# temporarily set global rate limit to 3000 rps
redis-cli -h rate-limiter set global_rps 3000
```
maria (oncall): deployed the route change? need exact command output.
sam (runtime): executed and validated. deploy-bot: 
"deploy-bot: route-change A-3301-R1 -> success (txn 7f3c)"
infra-api-bot: cache-warmup job submitted for prefixes [alpha_customer_1, beta_corp, gamma_saas] (job id: warm-3301). will stream status.
maria (oncall): applying temporary per-client soft throttles for bursty API keys. using ops tool.
alice (sre): I've also flipped fallback-instances: any queue item older than 5s gets routed to CPU-fallback pool (best-effort). This should reduce instantaneous GPU pressure but increase token-cost. Monitor p95 after 3m and note cost impact.
tiago (provisioning): parallel path: raising cloud support ticket for quota increase. created case CS-5543. ETA from provider support unknown (requested expedited). also asked infra to check if we have unused reservations that can be repurposed.
logs mid-mitigation:
```
[04:34] queue len=18000 p95=4.1s p99=15.9s
[04:36] route-change applied -> pool gpu-hosted-1 inflight decreased 32% -> queue growth slows
[04:38] cpu-fallback routing live -> p95 drops to 2.2s p99 7.8s
```
kevin (product): good. cs, please patch customers A, B, C with current mitigation steps + estimated recovery window. framing: we've enabled fallbacks and throttles; performance degraded but we are avoiding 100% failures.
customer-success: emailing affected accounts now. including A/B testing notes and ask for degraded-quality acceptance for next 4-6 hours. tagging enterprise accounts for priority escalation.
maria (oncall): monitoring. next steps if queue doesn't stabilize in 20m: consider controlled ingress shedding for best-effort tier, and region-level emergency re-route to us-west-2 where capacity is fine.
sam (runtime): adding guardrail: set ingress-shed trigger if queue growth rate > 10% over 5m AND p99 > 10s. command:
```
# temporary policy
redwoodctl set policy ingress_shed_us_east --thresholds "growth_5m:0.10,p99:10s,action:throttle_best_effort"
```
maria (oncall): after 12m of mitigations, metrics show stabilization. final snapshot:
```
[04:50] queue len=6200 p95=1.9s p99=5.6s gpu-inflight -45% vs peak
```
alice (sre): setting incident severity to Sev2 given partial customer impact but mitigation in place. adding follow-up action items: - permanently request quota increase for us-east-1 GPUs - add provider backoff for provisioner to avoid tight retries - add telemetry to correlate request-reties->provisioner storms
tiago (provisioning): noted. will request reservation repurpose and open PR for exponential backoff in provisioner.
maria (oncall): handing off to night oncall (alice). summary for handoff: root cause = cloud GPU quota + rate-limit causing autoscaler create failures -> queue growth -> p95/p99 spike. mitigations applied: routing to quantized small model, cpu-fallback routing, cache warmups, global soft rate limit, ingress-shed guardrail configured, provider support case CS-5543 opened. current status: stabilized but degraded. watch list: provider quota update, provisioner backoff PR, follow-up postmortem. handoff @alice (sre) : please ack and take pager.
alice (sre): ack. I'll monitor 3am-7am window and will escalate to infra if quota not granted by EOD. leaving playbook pinned.
maria (oncall): thanks all. logging final notes and starting incident timeline doc.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity=Sev2 | status=stabilized | assigned=alice (sre) | incident-id=INC-3301 | channel=incidents
